Patient: [NAME]  Age/Sex: 62/Female  MRN: [MRN]
Diagnosis: RIGHT EYE Mature Cataract
Procedure: RIGHT EYE Phacoemulsification with Foldable IOL + TA
PRESCRIBED MEDICATIONS
1. Loteprednol 0.5% Eye Drop
Dosage: 4 times/day × 2 weeks then taper
Instruction: Operated eye. Do not stop abruptly.
2. Gatifloxacin Eye Drop
Dosage: 4 times/day for 2 weeks
Instruction: Operated eye.
3. Refresh Tears / CMC 0.5%
Dosage: 4 times/day for 1 month
Instruction: Both eyes as needed for dryness.
4. Homide (Homatropine) Eye Drop
Dosage: 1 drop at night for 5 days
Instruction: Operated eye.
5. Tab. Ciprofloxacin 500 mg
Dosage: 1 tablet twice daily after food for 5 days
Instruction: Full course.
6. Tab. Diclofenac 50 mg
Dosage: 1 tablet twice daily after food for 3 days
Instruction: For pain/inflammation.
7. Cap. Omega-3
Dosage: 1 capsule daily for 1 month
Instruction: After meals.
GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS
• Always use a new bottle of eye drops after surgery. Do not share drops.
• Maintain at least 5 minutes gap between two different eye drops.
• Wash hands thoroughly before instilling eye drops.
• Avoid rubbing, pressing or touching the operated eye.
• Wear protective glasses / shield especially while sleeping for 1-2 weeks.
• Do not splash water directly into the eye for 1 week. Clean with boiled cooled water.
• Avoid heavy lifting, bending forward, and dusty environments for 2 weeks.
• Take oral medicines after food unless otherwise specified.
• Complete the full course of antibiotics even if you feel better.
• Report immediately if sudden decrease in vision, severe pain, or discharge occurs.

OPERATIVE REPORT & ANAESTHESIA RECORD
Patient: [NAME]  Age/Sex: 62/Female  MRN: [MRN]
Diagnosis: RIGHT EYE Mature Cataract
Procedure: RIGHT EYE Phacoemulsification with Foldable IOL + TA
Surgeon: Dr. Anil Mehta, MS (Ophth) Anaesthetist: Dr. Priya Verma, MD (Anaesth)
OPERATIVE REPORT
Pre-operative Diagnosis: As above.
Post-operative Diagnosis: Same.
Procedure Performed: As above under local anaesthesia.
Operative Findings & Technique:
• Patient positioned supine. Operated eye prepared and draped under sterile conditions.
• Peribulbar / topical anaesthesia administered. Speculum applied.
• Clear corneal incision (2.8 mm) made temporally / superiorly.
• Continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis performed with Utrata forceps.
• Hydrodissection and hydrodelineation carried out.
• Nucleus emulsified using phacoemulsification (stop-and-chop / divide-and-conquer).
• Cortical matter aspirated with irrigation-aspiration probe.
• Capsular bag filled with viscoelastic. Foldable IOL injected and positioned in the bag.
• IOL used: Spectraphob SPH-6, Power +19.50 D.
• Viscoelastic thoroughly removed. Incision hydrated / sutured if required.
• Subconjunctival antibiotic-steroid given. Eye patched.
Specimens: None.
Complications: None. Posterior capsule intact. No vitreous loss.
Estimated Blood Loss: Minimal.
Condition at end of procedure: Stable. IOL well centered. Eye quiet.
ANAESTHESIA REPORT
Type of Anaesthesia: Local (Peribulbar / Topical) with monitored anaesthesia care.
Airway: Spontaneous breathing. Oxygen via nasal cannula / face mask as reguired.
Monitoring: Continuous pulse oximetry, NIBP, ECG.
Medications Administered:
• Local anaesthetic: Lignocaine 2% + Bupivacaine 0.5% (peribulbar) / Topical proparacaine.
• Sedation (if used): Midazolam 1 mg IV / Fentanyl 25-50 mcg IV as needed.
• Antibiotic prophylaxis: as per institutional protocol.
Vital Signs: Remained stable throughout the procedure. No significant fluctuation.
Intra-operative Events: Uneventful.
Post-anaesthesia Condition: Awake, oriented, haemodynamically stable. Shifted to recovery.
Surgeon: Dr. Anil Mehta, MS (Ophth)
Anaesthetist: Dr. Priya Verma, MD (Anaesth)
